{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"2c7984f7d4004943dad4e4922f4e384d58bc142f3656eaeb61ea74706b415feb","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:59","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Braking, observation, lane checks and vehicle lights","heading":"C2 — Braking, observation, lane checks and vehicle lights","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Braking, observation, lane checks and vehicle lights

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A04
Looking well ahead reduces the need for abrupt stops and turns and the risk of striking another vehicle or being struck. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A04
Early observation allows gradual slowing and avoids unnecessary braking that wastes fuel. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A04
Acting on traffic changes early gives following drivers more reaction time and helps traffic flow steadily. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A04
Check to both sides for entering or crossing traffic, particularly at intersections and rail crossings. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A04
An intersection includes places where traffic merges or crosses, such as driveways and parking-area entrances as well as streets. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A04
Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians, checking again immediately before moving from a stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A04
Check that the path through an intersection is clear enough to avoid stopping and blocking it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A04
Before a left turn across opposing traffic, find a safe gap, check the receiving street for obstacles or pedestrians, and recheck approaching traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A04
Before turning right, check for vehicles from the left, opposing vehicles turning left and pedestrians in the turn path. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A04
Continue checking both cross-street directions even with a green light or priority sign because other road users may not obey their controls. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A04
If stopped with a blocked cross-street view, move forward slowly until you can see crossing traffic clearly. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A04
Look carefully to the sides near busy sidewalks, shops, parking areas, construction, playgrounds and schools because people or vehicles may enter the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A05
At any rail crossing, slow down and look along the tracks both ways; absence of previously seen trains does not mean no train is coming. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A05
Cross tracks only when there is room for the whole vehicle beyond them without blocking the crossing. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A05
At a multitrack crossing, wait until the first train is well beyond the crossing because it can conceal another train. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A05
Check rear traffic more often when traffic is heavy and particularly before changing lanes, slowing, reversing or descending a long or steep hill. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A05
Before changing lanes, merging from a ramp or entering from a curb or shoulder, check traffic alongside and behind the vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A05
Signal the intended lane change and use rear and side mirrors to confirm the target lane is clear and no one is about to pass. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A05
Look over the shoulder toward the planned move to check rear-corner blind spots that mirrors cannot show. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A05
Keep lane-change checks brief, rechecking as necessary while continuing to monitor the road ahead and the target lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A05
Use mirrors while preparing to merge or change lanes, then check over the shoulder immediately before moving. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A05
Check the lane beyond the target lane because another driver may be moving into the same space. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A06
Check behind whenever slowing, especially when braking quickly or slowing somewhere a following driver may not expect. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A06
Minimize reversing; a drive-through parking space can let you leave moving forward. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A06
Before entering a vehicle that must reverse, inspect behind it for children or objects not visible from the driver’s seat. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A06
When reversing, turn to look directly through the rear window rather than relying only on mirrors. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A06
Reverse slowly because steering is harder while backing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A06
Use an outside helper for reversing whenever possible. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A06
On long or steep descents, check mirrors and watch for trucks or buses gaining excessive speed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A06
Use high beams when opposing traffic is absent, while following traffic and heavy traffic call for low beams. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R31 | anchor: A06
High beams are useful on unfamiliar roads, in construction areas or near roadside pedestrians, subject to the requirement to dim for approaching traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R32 | anchor: A06
Dim high beams by the time an opposing vehicle is within 500 feet. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R33 | anchor: A06
Use low beams while following another vehicle or driving in heavy traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R34 | anchor: A06
Use low beams in fog, snow or heavy rain because reflected high-beam light can produce glare. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R35 | anchor: A06
Headlights must be on in rain, mist and snow and whenever the wipers are operating. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R36 | anchor: A06
Do not drive using parking lights alone. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R37 | anchor: A06
If an approaching driver uses high beams, briefly flash the headlights a couple of times. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec13-R38 | anchor: A06
If the other driver does not dim, look toward the right roadway edge and avoid retaliating with high beams. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0119]
